# inbrix `/v1` API — the PIM contract

`/v1` is inbrix's stable, machine-readable **contract**: JSON mail + calendar +
contacts served over one HTTP surface. inbrix is a standalone PIM client — it
connects to the **user's own** IMAP/SMTP/CalDAV/CardDAV account and exposes what
it reads/writes there as `/v1`. It hosts no mail server and depends on no central
server. When the local SQLite mirror is enabled, one application account may own
several mailboxes; the active mailbox selected in the session scopes each `/v1`
mail request.

`/v1` is the shared source of truth other UIs build on:

- the **Vulos OS** thin Calendar/Contacts widgets and mail surface consume it;
- inbrix's own React browser client is a first-class consumer too;
- any third-party tool or script can drive it.

The API returns `models.Email` / `MailboxInfo` / `models.Calendar*` /
`models.Contact` JSON and never renders HTML, so it is a stable seam an
external UI can build against. It is the backend used by the React SPA and shares the
same engine + authentication — using `/v1` never changes the standalone UI.

> **Stability.** `/v1` is load-bearing: external UIs build on it. The mail,
> `/v1/calendar/*`, and `/v1/contacts` shapes are treated as a stable contract —
> changes are additive.

## Authentication

inbrix can be used without an application account through direct mailbox login.
With the local SQLite mirror enabled, it also provides a local application
account (`/register` and `/user-login`) whose password is separate from mailbox
passwords. A user can attach several own mailboxes and switch the active one;
every `/v1` route remains owner-scoped by the authenticated user. There is no
account/tenant/user path segment; API keys may select an owned mailbox through
the validated `X-Account-ID` header described below. The
*only* remote credentials are still the user's own IMAP/SMTP password or an
OAuth2 access token for their provider.

Requests can authenticate in three ways:

| Mode | How the caller proves itself | Who uses it |
|------|------------------------------|-------------|
| **User API key** | `Authorization: Bearer inbrix_live_…` or `X-API-Key: inbrix_live_…` | scripts and integrations acting as a local application user |
| **Session cookie** (default) | The cookie set by `POST /login`, `POST /user-login`, or the OAuth2 callback | browsers, `curl -b cookies.txt`, inbrix's React client |
| **Injected credentials** (opt-in, off by default) | `X-Vulos-Broker-Auth` + `X-Vulos-Mail-*` headers | an embedding host that already holds the user's mailbox credentials |

User API keys are available when local application accounts are enabled. A key
inherits all of its owner's current backend permissions, including API key
management. Existing ownership checks and super-administrator restrictions apply
unchanged, and role changes take effect on the next request. A key never grants
access to another user's mailbox or private data.

Create and manage keys under **Settings → API Keys**. Complete secrets are shown
only when created or rotated; the database stores only SHA-256 hashes and public
prefixes. Keys may expire, can be revoked immediately, and support rotation that
atomically invalidates the previous key. The UI lists recent usage time/IP and
creation, rotation, and revocation events.

```sh
# INBRIX_API_KEY contains the secret copied when the key was created.
curl http://localhost:3001/api/capabilities \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INBRIX_API_KEY"

curl http://localhost:3001/v1/me \
  -H "X-API-Key: $INBRIX_API_KEY"
```

Key authentication works on the existing protected backend routes (including
`/api/*` and `/v1/*`); a separate copy of the API is not needed. Requests use the
owner's default mailbox unless `X-Account-ID` selects another mailbox owned by
the same user. Selection is request-local and does not switch any browser
session. An explicit invalid, expired, or revoked key returns `401`, even if a
valid browser cookie is also present. Keys are accepted only in headers.

Only **verified** key requests skip browser CSRF checks. Cookie-authenticated
mutations still require a valid CSRF cookie and matching `X-CSRF-Token`. API key
requests do not create persistent login sessions or issue login cookies.

API key management endpoints (all scoped to the authenticated user):

| Method | Path | Body / result |
|--------|------|---------------|
| GET | `/api/settings/api-keys` | `{ "keys": [...] }`, metadata only |
| POST | `/api/settings/api-keys` | `{ "name": "automation", "expiresAt": null }`; returns metadata and one-time `key` |
| POST | `/api/settings/api-keys/:id/rotate` | Returns a new key, preserving name and expiration; old key stops working |
| POST | `/api/settings/api-keys/:id/revoke` | Optional `{ "reason": "..." }`; returns `{ "ok": true }` |
| GET | `/api/settings/api-keys/:id/events` | `{ "events": [...] }`, latest 100 operations |

`expiresAt` may be null (no expiration) or a future RFC3339 timestamp. Names are
required and limited to 120 characters. Key-management responses use `no-store`.
There is no API-key refresh endpoint; expired or revoked keys cannot be rotated.

Browser and broker requests continue using their existing authentication. The
local SQLite mirror is used by the inbox path; `/v1` continues to expose the live
mail engine contract.

When no valid authentication is provided, the API responds **`401` with a
JSON body**, so a `fetch()`-based client can react in code:

```json
{ "error": "not authenticated" }
```

Send requests with credentials included (e.g. `fetch(url, { credentials: 'include' })`).

### Automation discovery and application mailboxes

An AI client can start with `GET /api/automation` using its API key. This returns
authentication and mailbox-selection instructions, the selected mailbox, a link
to `/api/capabilities`, and a paginated list of the running server's registered
`/api/*` and `/v1/*` operations. The list comes from the actual router, so disabled
calendar/contact routes are absent. Discovery requires authentication and works
even before the user has attached a mailbox.

Each operation has `method`, `path` (a Fiber route template such as `:uid`),
`pathParameters`, and `readOnly`. Where this document contains an endpoint table,
`reference` includes its section, table header and row with query/body/response
hints. These hints are **not OpenAPI/JSON Schema**. An absent reference means
the parameter contract is not documented in this catalog; clients should not
guess request bodies. Listing a route does not grant permission to execute it;
ordinary users still receive `403` on administrator-only operations. Registered
features can also return `501`/`503` when their backing services are unavailable.

Filter by `q` (case-insensitive substring of method, path or reference), `method`,
or exact route-template `path`. `limit` defaults to 50 (maximum 100), `offset`
defaults to zero, and `nextOffset` is null when there are no further results.
Fetch detailed prose/examples using
`/api/automation/reference?section=<reference.section>` (URL-encoded). Omit
`section` to download the complete Markdown reference embedded in this build.

For **application mailboxes**, first call `GET /api/accounts`: it returns a JSON
array including each owned mailbox's stable `id`, `email`, `label` and
`is_default`, without credentials. Send that `id` in `X-Account-ID` on **every**
mailbox request, including search, pagination, detail, attachments and writes.
The API key is user-level: the same key can operate all mailboxes owned by that
user. Foreign or unknown IDs return `404`. Without the header, every request
uses the user's current default mailbox. `/api/accounts/:id/switch` only changes
the current request for key authentication; it cannot persist selection between
requests. Explicit headers allow concurrent automation against different
mailboxes without changing a browser's active mailbox.

Message UIDs are only unique within a folder of one mailbox: keep
`(accountId, folder, uid)` together. To search across all application mailboxes,
enumerate `/api/accounts`, search each with its explicit `X-Account-ID`, and
retain those identifiers in merged results. `/v1/accounts` and `/v1/unified`
use the **separate legacy connected-account store**; they do not enumerate or
aggregate the SQLite application's mailbox list.

| Method | Path | Query | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|-------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/api/automation` | `q?`, `method?`, `path?`, `limit?`, `offset?` | — | `{ version, authentication, mailboxes, capabilitiesEndpoint, referenceEndpoint, instructions, total, limit, offset, nextOffset, operations }` |
| `GET` | `/api/automation/reference` | `section?` | — | Markdown reference or one section; unknown section is `404` |
| `GET` | `/api/capabilities` | — | — | `{ notifications, webPush, calendar, role, currentUser }` |
| `GET` | `/api/accounts` | — | — | Owned application mailbox array: `[{ id, email, label, color?, is_default, imap_server, imap_port, smtp_server, smtp_port }]` |
| `GET` | `/api/mail/folders` | — | — | Locally mirrored folders for the selected mailbox |
| `GET` | `/api/mail/messages` | `folder` (required), `limit?`, `offset?` | — | `{ folder, messages, limit, offset, nextOffset, syncComplete, syncError?, lastSyncAt? }` |
| `GET` | `/api/mail/messages/:uid` | `folder` (required) | — | `Email` with optional `mailSummary`, `mailTranslation`, `mailTranslationAll`; `409` if body is not cached yet |
| `PATCH` | `/api/mail/messages/:uid/read` | `folder` (required) | — | `{ ok, updated, sync }`; queues a read-status update for the selected mailbox |
| `GET` | `/api/mail/search` | `q` (required), `limit?` | — | `{ query, terms, hasMore, results }`; searches the selected mailbox's cached conversation mail (inbox/sent and pending/draft sends) |

Example startup and mailbox-specific read:

```sh
curl "$INBRIX_URL/api/automation?q=messages&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INBRIX_API_KEY"

curl "$INBRIX_URL/api/accounts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INBRIX_API_KEY"

# INBRIX_ACCOUNT_ID is an id returned by /api/accounts.
curl "$INBRIX_URL/api/mail/messages?folder=INBOX&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INBRIX_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Account-ID: $INBRIX_ACCOUNT_ID"
```

### Injected-credential mode (embedding hosts)

Normally inbrix holds its own session and connects to the user's mailbox itself.
As an **option**, an embedding host (or the test harness) may inject the
per-request connection descriptor as HTTP headers, so inbrix builds the IMAP/
SMTP/DAV client **directly from the headers** instead of from a session. These
headers only ever describe the **user's own** account (endpoint + a short-lived
OAuth token or password) that inbrix then talks to — inbrix hosts no mail and
depends on no central server.

This path is **off by default** and gated by a shared secret:

- Set `INBRIX_BROKER_SECRET` (environment variable) on the inbrix process.
- Every request must send `X-Vulos-Broker-Auth: <secret>`. inbrix compares it
  against `INBRIX_BROKER_SECRET` in **constant time**.
- **If `INBRIX_BROKER_SECRET` is unset, or the presented secret does not match,
  the `X-Vulos-Mail-*` headers are ignored entirely** and the request falls back
  to normal session auth. Standalone inbrix therefore never trusts arbitrary
  client-supplied connection headers.

When the secret validates, inbrix reads the connection spec from these headers:

| Header | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Provider`  | `gmail` \| `outlook` \| `imap` (informational) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Email`     | mailbox address (used as MAIL FROM / identity) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Username`  | IMAP/SMTP login username (defaults to the email) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Auth`      | `xoauth2` (access token) \| `plain` (password) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Secret`    | the XOAUTH2 access token, or the IMAP/SMTP password |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Imap-Host` | IMAP host (required) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Imap-Port` | IMAP port (default `993`, implicit TLS) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Smtp-Host` | SMTP host (defaults to the IMAP host) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Smtp-Port` | SMTP port (default `587`; `465` ⇒ implicit TLS, else STARTTLS) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Caldav-Url`  | CalDAV base URL for the account (optional; enables `/v1/calendar/*`) |
| `X-Vulos-Mail-Carddav-Url` | CardDAV base URL for the account (optional; enables `/v1/contacts`) |

`xoauth2` builds the IMAP client via `NewClientOAuth(host, port, username, token,
"xoauth2")` and the SMTP client via `NewSMTPClientOAuth`; `plain` uses
`NewClient(host, port, username, password)` / `NewSMTPClient`. This path covers
the mail routes — folders, messages, single message, search, flags, delete, move,
compose (`POST /v1/messages`) and drafts (`POST /v1/drafts`).

**Calendar & contacts.** When `X-Vulos-Mail-Caldav-Url` /
`X-Vulos-Mail-Carddav-Url` are present, the `/v1/calendar/*` and `/v1/contacts`
routes are served from those per-account DAV base URLs instead of the session.
Authentication reuses `X-Vulos-Mail-Auth: xoauth2` + `X-Vulos-Mail-Secret`: the
access token is presented to CalDAV/CardDAV as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` header. If the relevant DAV URL header is **absent**, the read routes
return an empty result (`{ "events": [] }` / `{ "busy": [] }` /
`{ "contacts": [] }`) and the write routes return `501 Not Implemented` — the
session is never touched. These routes are registered whenever CalDAV/CardDAV is
enabled in config **or** the injected-credential path is active
(`INBRIX_BROKER_SECRET` set).

Note: Outlook/Microsoft 365 calendar & contacts (Microsoft Graph) are **not**
covered by this CalDAV/CardDAV path; only accounts that expose CalDAV/CardDAV
(e.g. Gmail, generic DAV) work here.

The headers are only ever read **inside** the `/v1` group, after the secret has
been validated — never on unauthenticated paths.

**The exact wire format** — header-by-header semantics, the acceptance algorithm,
and an explicit list of the properties this scheme does *not* have (no HMAC, no
timestamp window, no nonce, no replay protection) — is specified in
[SIGNING.md § 1](signing.md#1-mail-broker-seam-inbound). Read it before deploying
the seam: it is only safe over a trusted transport.

> **No webhooks.** inbrix never calls out to a URL you supply. There is no
> webhook registration surface, no event delivery, and no outbound signature
> scheme — see [SIGNING.md § 0](signing.md#0-inbrix-emits-no-webhooks) for what
> to use instead (SSE, Web Push, or polling).

## Product library (`/api/products`)

With the local SQLite mirror enabled, product records, categories and images
belong to the authenticated application user. They are shared across that
user's mailboxes and work before a mailbox is attached. `X-Account-ID` does not
change the library owner. All routes accept browser sessions or API keys;
browser writes require CSRF. A foreign product, category or image returns `404`.

| Method | Path | Query / body / result |
|--------|------|-----------------------|
| GET | `/api/product-dimensions` | Owner-scoped shared definitions: `{dimensions:[{key,label,type,unit,options,version,productCount,updatedAt}]}` |
| POST | `/api/product-dimensions` | `{label,type,unit,options}`; `201 {dimension}` with a server-generated key |
| PUT | `/api/product-dimensions/:key` | `{label,type,unit,options,version}`; updates canonical definition and referencing product versions; stale version `409` |
| DELETE | `/api/product-dimensions/:key` | Required `version`; unused definitions only; `{ok:true}` |
| GET | `/api/product-categories` | `{categories:[{id,name,parentId,productCount}]}` (direct counts) |
| POST | `/api/product-categories` | `{name,parentId?}`; returns `{category}` |
| PUT | `/api/product-categories/:id` | `{name,parentId?}`; rename or move an owned category; omitted parent preserves hierarchy |
| DELETE | `/api/product-categories/:id` | Leaf categories only; uncategorizes products and advances their versions; `{ok:true}` |
| GET | `/api/product-navigation` | `{brands:[{name,productCount,categories:[{categoryId,productCount}]}],total}` for the complete owned library; empty brand/category IDs mean unbranded/uncategorized |
| GET | `/api/products` | `q`, `categoryId` (includes descendants), `brand` (exact; empty = unbranded; omitted = all), `uncategorized=true`, `limit` (default 10, 1–20), `offset` (default 0, 0–100000); bounded product search page |
| GET | `/api/products/search` | Same parameters and response as `/api/products` |
| POST | `/api/products` | Product input below; `201 {product}` |
| GET | `/api/products/:id` | `{product}` including complete specification, for the management editor |
| PUT | `/api/products/:id` | Complete product input including current `version`; `{product}`; stale version `409` |
| DELETE | `/api/products/:id` | Required query `version`; `{ok:true}`; stale version `409` |
| GET | `/api/products/:id/read` | `version` (recommended), `offset` (Unicode characters, default 0), `length` (default 2400, 1–4000); bounded specification read; version conflict `409` |
| POST | `/api/products/query-prices` | Structured configuration and price query described below; read-only despite POST |
| GET | `/api/product-price-imports` | Pending legacy price rows, `offset` (default 0), `limit` (default 30, 1–100); `{rows,total,hasMore,nextOffset}` |
| POST | `/api/product-price-imports/:id` | Explicitly import one pending row: `{productId,version,price?}`; empty productId creates a product; returns `{product}` |
| GET | `/api/product-images/:id` | Owner-authenticated PNG/JPEG bytes; private, no-store |

Product input is `{name,brand,model,categoryId,specification,version,imageDataUrl?,catalog?}`.
`name` is required (max 200 characters), `brand` max 100, `model` max 160.
`categoryId` is an owned category ID or empty. `specification` is one Markdown
text field (max 100,000 Unicode characters), including parameters, tables,
conditions and source references. `version` is required on update. Omit
`imageDataUrl` to keep the current image, send an empty string to remove it, or
send a PNG/JPEG base64 data URL (decoded size at most 2 MiB, max 16 megapixels).
Images are stored in SQLite under immutable owner-scoped IDs. The UI resizes
uploads. Category names are required, unique per user, max 100 characters.

Search returns `{products,total,hasMore,nextOffset}`. Each hit contains product
metadata, `version`, `imageId`/`imageUrl`, `section`, `heading`, Unicode `offset`
and an excerpt of at most 400 characters. Full specifications and image bytes
are excluded. Empty `q` enumerates products. Nonempty queries use SQLite FTS5
with Chinese character/bigram tokens, Latin words and normalized model matching
(e.g. `KE-43` can be found using `ke43`). Terms are ANDed within an indexed
section; this is **not** semantic search or numerical range filtering. Repeat
the same query/brand/category and use `nextOffset` to continue. Counts/offset pages
reflect current data, so concurrent edits may change page boundaries.

Reads return `{product,sections,sectionCount,hasMoreSections,content,offset,
nextOffset,hasMore,totalLength}` without the full specification in `product`.
The section directory includes at most 20 sections starting at the section
containing the requested content offset. Each section has an index, heading,
Unicode offset and length; use offsets to continue reading sections/table
headers. The text is retained exactly, including original tables and units.
Updates rebuild chunks and the full-text index in the same transaction.
Only the current specification is retained; versions detect changed evidence,
not a historical specification archive.

### Brand and category navigation

The product library uses a left navigation panel and a right product table.
Brands are grouped from the product's existing independent `brand` field.
Below each brand, the shared category hierarchy shows only categories containing
that brand's products and their ancestors. Counts in navigation include descendants;
`product-categories.productCount` remains a direct count. Navigation aggregates
are independent of search text and result pagination. On narrow screens the same
navigation opens in a dialog, leaving the table its full width. The table fills
the remaining height and scrolls internally with a fixed header and pagination.

`parentId` is empty for a top-level category. Existing categories migrate as roots
without changing product references or versions. Parents must belong to the owner;
self/descendant parents are rejected. Category names remain unique per owner.
Omitting `parentId` on update preserves its current parent; sending an empty string
moves it to the top level. A category with children cannot be deleted until they
are moved or deleted. Selecting a parent filters over its entire subtree and can
be combined with an exact brand. Brands share category definitions rather than
duplicating them. New product drafts inherit the selected brand/category.

### Structured configurations and pricing

The product editor owns both the narrative document and its structured catalog.
The standalone price-list UI and `/api/price-lists` routes have been retired;
old browser bookmarks open the product library's pending-price workflow.
Original price-list tables remain intact as migration source data. Pending rows
are excluded from AI pricing until explicitly linked. Importing a row and
marking it resolved is one transaction, so retries cannot duplicate products.
The UI lets users review and correct the CNY unit price.
Unmapped original columns remain available in the source record; ordinary
custom specification columns are imported as dimensions. `notes` remains in the
source archive rather than becoming a configuration dimension. Importing into
an existing product requires complete values for its dimension definitions.

### Shared specification dimensions

Definitions are maintained once per application owner in the product library's
shared-dimensions manager. Products select only the relevant dimensions and
store configuration values under their stable keys. Global means shared across
that user's products and mailboxes, not across different users. A dimension's
identity includes its name, type and case-sensitive unit (MPa differs from mPa).
The same name with different types/units may exist in the dictionary; select the
correct definition explicitly. Duplicate identities are rejected.

Product catalog input can use `dimensions:[{key:"..."}]`. Existing keys resolve
to canonical definitions; copied labels, types and units cannot override the
shared dictionary. GET product and AI pricing results return resolved definitions.
For backward compatibility, inline definitions with unknown keys are promoted
into the dictionary and equivalent definitions are reused with attributes remapped.
Existing local definitions migrate transactionally on upgrade; actual values,
variant IDs and price IDs are preserved. Legacy select options are unioned when
merging equivalent definitions so no existing option is lost.

Renaming a definition or updating its options updates every referencing product,
rebuilds its search metadata, and advances its product version in one transaction.
Changing the type or unit of a used definition, removing a used option, or
renaming it to cause a product-level dimension-label collision is rejected (400).
Used definitions cannot be deleted. Unused definitions can change type/unit or
be deleted with their current version. Tombstones prevent stale product drafts
from recreating a deleted definition. Foreign-owner definitions return 404.
Saved quotation/contract snapshots remain intact; new AI queries must use the
new product version after a shared-definition edit.

The product editor shows selected dimension chips with remove icons and an
"Add dimension" button. Its shadcn Base UI DropdownMenu adds the selected shared
definition immediately; already selected definitions are omitted. Loading, empty
and retry states appear only inside the dropdown. Global definitions are created
from the library's separate manager. The editor uses Base UI Select for variant
values and AlertDialog for removing dimensions with existing configuration data.
Removing a dimension only removes its selection and draft values, not the shared
definition.

### Product catalog input

`catalog` is optional on save: omitting it preserves the existing catalog;
`{dimensions:[],variants:[]}` explicitly clears it. Product version checks cover
narrative, definitions, configurations and prices atomically. GET by ID returns
the complete catalog for management; text search/read omit full catalogs.
Structured attribute values and SKUs are indexed for product discovery.

```json
{
  "dimensions": [
    {"key":"connection","label":"连接方式","type":"select","unit":"","options":["法兰","螺纹"]},
    {"key":"diameter","label":"口径","type":"number","unit":"mm"}
  ],
  "variants": [
    {"id":"","sku":"BV-F50","attributes":{"connection":"法兰","diameter":"50"},
     "prices":[{"id":"","amount":"1280.00"}]}
  ]
}
```

Stable dimension keys survive label edits. Types are `text`, `number`, `select`;
every actual variant must supply every defined dimension. Do not generate the
Cartesian product of option values. A simple product has zero dimensions and
one default variant. Limits: 40 dimensions, 500 variants, 50 prices per variant.
New variants/prices use empty IDs; the server generates IDs. Existing supplied
IDs must belong to that same product/variant. Duplicate configurations and
nonempty SKUs are rejected. Amounts are decimal strings (0 allowed, up to six
decimal places), always in CNY. Currency and pricing unit are not editable fields.
Responses include fixed `currency:"CNY"` metadata for compatibility with AI clients;
omitted currency defaults to CNY and foreign-currency writes are rejected.
Legacy pricing units are ignored; specification dimension units remain intact.
Tax mode is `included`, `excluded`, or empty (unknown); a known mode requires an
explicit decimal tax rate between 0 and 1. Quantity intervals are inclusive.
Validity dates are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` dates; a missing bound is open-ended.

POST `/api/products/query-prices` accepts
`{productId,version?,variantId?,priceId?,attributes?,qty?,source?,date?,limit?,offset?}`.
An empty attributes map discovers dimensions and actual configurations. Filter
using stable dimension keys and exact text values (case-insensitive); numeric
values are normalized, without unit conversion or range inference. Alternatively
use `{query}` for keyword discovery, then select productId for attribute filters.
The date defaults to the current UTC date. Limits are 1–50 (default 10), offsets
0–100000. Counts and status include all candidates before pagination.

The result is `{status,dimensions,matches,missing,total,hasMore,nextOffset}`.
Each match includes productId/productVersion, product name/model, variantId,
SKU, complete attributes and all applicable price records with stable IDs.
`matched` means one configuration and one applicable price with all dimension
values supplied (or an explicitly selected variantId). priceId can filter an
explicitly selected price and requires productId and variantId. `needs_clarification` means additional configuration/price
conditions must be resolved; a single returned page is not proof of uniqueness.
`no_match` means no configuration matched; `no_price` means configurations exist
but have no applicable price under the supplied quantity, source and date.
Unknown dimensions and invalid quantities/dates return 400; stale version 409;
foreign products return 404. An empty price is never interpreted as zero.

The editor maintains one CNY unit price per configuration, with no price-condition
controls or CSV import/export. Clearing the amount removes the price; zero remains
a valid price. Existing legacy records and conditions are preserved until the user
re-enters that configuration's amount, replacing them with one unconditional price.
API price arrays and query filters remain compatible with archived records.
Tax treatment is unspecified for newly entered plain prices; no tax rate is inferred.
Legacy price migration also reuses an unambiguous compatible shared definition; unknown units or
ambiguous names require selecting a product rather than guessing a mapping.

Catalog-priced document items include `productId`, `productVersion`, `variantId`,
`priceId` and `qty`. Generation verifies ownership, current version, configuration,
price validity and quantity conditions, then fills the exact stored amount and
recomputes line amounts. Currency conflicts are rejected. Catalog tax treatment
replaces the legacy default tax surcharge; unknown tax terms leave final tax
and total fields unconfirmed. Configuration and price references survive saved
quotation/contract canvas documents, including items without product images.


The built-in email/document AI gains `list_product_categories`,
`search_products`, `read_product`, and `query_product_prices` (`lookup_price`
is a compatibility alias for the product catalog). `read_product` requires the version
returned by search. Tool results and the existing total context budget are
bounded. Search only locates candidates: the agent must read limits and
configuration conditions, distinguish supported/contradicted/unknown
requirements, cite product/version/section, and state incomplete coverage.
User-maintained reference text is data, not executable instructions.

AI quotation/contract items can specify `productId` and `productVersion` from
the library. The server validates ownership/version and resolves `picture`
to the stored immutable image URL. Images are rendered in quotation picture
cells and contract description cells. Saved documents retain their text and
image references when products are changed or deleted. Old image blobs remain
available to their owner for these references; a product deletion does not
garbage-collect them. Product specifications do not establish commercial prices;
the existing price-list and mail tools remain available for the relevant source.

## Conventions

- **Folders** travel as the `folder` query parameter (default `INBOX`). This
  avoids escaping the IMAP hierarchy delimiter — `?folder=INBOX/Archive` works
  verbatim.
- **UIDs** are numeric and appear as path segments.
- **Pagination** on `/v1/messages`: `limit` caps the page size and `offset` skips
  the newest N messages, so page *k* = `?limit=L&offset=k*L`. The response echoes
  the effective `limit`/`offset` and sets `nextOffset` to the next page's offset
  (`null` when the returned page was short, i.e. the end of the mailbox).
- Errors are always `{ "error": "<message>" }` with an appropriate status code
  (`400` bad request, `401` unauthenticated, `404` not found, `409` conflict,
  `429` rate-limited, `501` not implemented, `502` upstream mail-server failure).
- All payloads follow the `models.Email` / `MailboxInfo` shapes (see
  `models/email.go`, `handlers/api/client.go`).

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Query | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|-------|------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/v1/me`                       | —                       | —              | `{ email, username }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/folders`                  | —                       | —              | `{ folders: MailboxInfo[] }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/folders`                  | —                       | `{ name }`     | `201 { folder }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/folders`                  | `folder`                | `{ name }` (or `?folder=`) | `204` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/messages`                 | `folder`, `limit` (50), `offset` (0) | —  | `{ folder, limit, offset, nextOffset, messages: Email[] }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/messages/:uid`            | `folder`                | —              | `Email` (incl. `attachments[]`) |
| `GET`    | `/v1/messages/:uid/attachments/:partId` | `folder`       | —              | attachment bytes (streamed) |
| `GET`    | `/v1/search`                   | `folder`, `q`, `limit` (100) | —         | `{ folder, query, messages: Email[] }` |
| `PATCH`  | `/v1/messages/:uid/flags`      | `folder`                | `{ flag, add }` or `{ flags[], add }` | `204` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/messages/:uid`            | `folder`, `hard`        | —              | `204` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/messages/:uid/move`       | `folder`                | `{ toFolder, folder? }` | `204` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/messages/:uid/spam`       | `folder`                | —              | `{ folder }` (Junk/Spam target) |
| `POST`   | `/v1/messages/:uid/snooze`     | `folder`                | `{ until }`    | `200 { snoozed, autoReturn:false, until, folder, note }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/messages/:uid/snooze`     | `folder`                | —              | `204` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/messages`                 | —                       | `{ to, cc?, bcc?, subject, text?, html?, inReplyTo?, attachments?, sendAt? }`¹ | `201 { sent: true }`, or `202 { scheduled, id, sendAt }` when `sendAt` is set |
| `POST`   | `/v1/drafts`                   | —                       | `{ to?, cc?, subject?, text?, html?, inReplyTo?, attachments? }`¹     | `201 { saved: true }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/attachments`              | —                       | multipart form, file field `file` | `201 { token, filename, size, contentType }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/scheduled`                | —                       | —              | `{ scheduled: […] }` (pending send-later) |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/scheduled/:id`            | —                       | —              | `204` |
| `PATCH`  | `/v1/scheduled/:id`            | —                       | `{ sendAt?, subject?, text?, html?, to?, cc?, bcc? }` | updated record |

¹ Each entry of `attachments[]` is `{ token? , data? , filename?, contentType?, contentId?, inline? }`
— see [Attachments](api.md#attachments) for the two-step upload flow and `cid:` inline images.

`POST /v1/folders` creates an IMAP mailbox (a "label" in the mail UI); the name
may not contain the IMAP control characters `\r \n \t * % "` and may not collide
with a protected system folder (Inbox/Sent/Drafts/Spam/Trash/Archive/Snoozed/…),
which return `409`. `DELETE /v1/folders` deletes a user mailbox by `name` (body)
or `?folder=`; system folders are `403`.

`POST /v1/messages/:uid/spam` reports spam by moving the message to the
discovered Junk/Spam folder — there is no separate training-signal endpoint on
this backend, so the move IS the report (pair it with an undo toast like archive).

`POST /v1/messages/:uid/snooze` moves the message to the Snoozed folder and
validates + echoes `until`. inbrix is a client and does not itself run a
delivery-side scheduler, so it does **not** auto-return the message to the inbox:
the response is `200 { snoozed:true, autoReturn:false, until, folder, note }` and
the client is responsible for surfacing the due time / returning the message.
`DELETE /v1/messages/:uid/snooze` is a no-op acknowledgement kept for symmetry
(the caller moves the message back itself); it returns `204`.

`DELETE /v1/messages/:uid` MOVES the message to the Trash folder by default
(discovered via the `\Trash` special-use, with name fallbacks Trash / Deleted /
Deleted Items / Bin). Pass `?hard=true` (or `?hard=1`) to permanently expunge
instead. If the source folder already IS the Trash folder, or no Trash folder
can be located, the delete falls back to a permanent expunge.

`POST /v1/messages/:uid/move` moves a message between folders (e.g. archive).
The source folder comes from the `folder` query param (default `INBOX`); an
optional non-empty `folder` field in the body overrides it. `toFolder` is
required.

`POST /v1/messages` is **rate-limited per client IP** to prevent spam/relay abuse
(default 30 sends / 60 s, configurable via `[rate_limit]` in `config.toml`); the
cap returns `429 { "error": "rate limit exceeded" }`.

### Attachments

**Download.** `GET /v1/messages/:uid/attachments/:partId?folder=` streams a
single MIME part on demand (the content is NOT included in the message listing).
`partId` is the IMAP MIME part path — take it from an entry's `partId` in the
message's `attachments[]` array (see the `Email` shape below). The response
carries the part's `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition: attachment;
filename="…"` (with an RFC 5987 `filename*` form for non-ASCII names). Both the
content type and filename are sanitized against response-header injection; an
untrusted/malformed content type falls back to `application/octet-stream`.
Downloads are capped at 25 MiB. Works in both session and injected-credential modes.
Unknown part / message ⇒ `404`; unauthenticated ⇒ `401`.

**Upload (compose).** Attaching a file to an outgoing message is a two-step,
JSON-friendly flow:

1. `POST /v1/attachments` — multipart form with a `file` field. Stages the bytes
   under the caller's per-account namespace and returns
   `201 { token, filename, size, contentType }`.
2. `POST /v1/messages` (or `/v1/drafts`) — reference the staged upload in the
   `attachments` array: `{"attachments":[{"token":"<token>"}]}`. Each token is
   resolved and CONSUMED (single-use, so it cannot be replayed). `filename` /
   `contentType` may be supplied per-entry to override the staged metadata.

Alternatively, small files can be sent fully inline (no step 1) with
`{"filename":"a.txt","contentType":"text/plain","data":"<base64>"}`. A single
attachment (and the per-message total) is capped at 25 MiB. Staged uploads that
are never sent are garbage-collected after 24 h.

**Inline images (`cid:`).** To embed an image *inside* the HTML body (rather than
send it as a downloadable file), mark the attachment ref `inline` and give it a
`contentId`, then reference that id from the HTML with `<img src="cid:ID">`:

```json
{
  "to": "bob@example.com",
  "subject": "Hi",
  "html": "<p>See <img src=\"cid:logo1\"></p>",
  "attachments": [
    { "contentId": "logo1", "inline": true,
      "contentType": "image/png", "data": "<base64>" }
  ]
}
```

The two new per-entry fields extend the existing attachment ref shape:

| field       | type    | meaning |
|-------------|---------|---------|
| `contentId` | string  | Bare cid token — **no** `cid:` scheme, **no** angle brackets. Must match the `cid:ID` in the HTML. Required when `inline`. Validated against header injection (`[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+(@host)?`; CRLF/space/`<>"` rejected). |
| `inline`    | boolean | `true` ⇒ the part is emitted with `Content-Disposition: inline` and a `Content-ID: <contentId>` header inside a `multipart/related` container, so it renders in-body. |

`inline` and the byte source are orthogonal: an inline image can be supplied by
`token` (staged upload) **or** by base64 `data`. An `inline` ref without a
`contentId` is a `400`; an `inline` ref on a message with no `html` body degrades
to a normal attachment (nothing could reference it).

Resulting MIME structure:

- **inline only** → `multipart/related( multipart/alternative(text, html), inline-parts… )`
- **inline + regular attachments** →
  `multipart/mixed( multipart/related( multipart/alternative(text, html), inline-parts… ), attachments… )`
- **no inline parts** → unchanged (`multipart/mixed`/`alternative`/plain as before).

This lets clients avoid shipping fat `data:image/…;base64,…` URIs inside the HTML
body (which inflate every message ~33 %) and reference `cid:` parts instead. The
web composer inserts CID images from its image picker, clipboard, and drag/drop.
New images are proportionally sized so their longest edge is at most 480 pixels;
the editor resize handle can then set a larger proportional `width`/`height`.

### Scheduled send (send-later)

`POST /v1/messages` with a **future** RFC3339 `sendAt` turns an ordinary send into
a scheduled one: the compose payload is persisted and delivered at the due time by
a background drain, and the call returns `202 { scheduled:true, id, sendAt }`
instead of `201 { sent:true }`. Omit `sendAt` (or pass an empty string) for an
immediate send. A past/absurd `sendAt` is `400`; a value beyond one year is `400`.
For accounts authenticated with a short-lived OAuth token (injected Gmail/Outlook creds,
or a session OAuth login) the horizon tightens to ~12 h — beyond that the captured
token would be expired at fire time, so the schedule is refused up front rather
than accepted and silently failed.

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/v1/scheduled`      | —                                          | `{ scheduled: [{ id, sendAt, to, cc?, bcc?, subject, created }] }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/scheduled/:id`  | —                                          | `204` |
| `PATCH`  | `/v1/scheduled/:id`  | `{ sendAt?, subject?, text?, html?, to?, cc?, bcc? }` (all optional) | updated public record |

Scheduled sends are scoped to the authenticated account: another account's `id`
(or a nonexistent one) is `404`, so listing/cancel/edit never leak across
accounts. Delivery is **at-least-once** — the record is deleted only after a
successful SMTP send, so a crash mid-send re-fires it on the next poll (a rare
duplicate) rather than dropping the mail; a persistently failing send is abandoned
after a bounded retry budget. Every fire rebuilds the MIME through the same
`BuildMIMEMessage` engine as an immediate send, so the header-injection guard and
`cid:` inline handling run at actual send time.

Scheduled send is **enabled by wiring a durable KV store** into the API handler
(`NewWithStore`). Where it is not configured, `POST /v1/messages` with `sendAt`
and the whole `/v1/scheduled` surface return `501 Not Implemented` — an
unconfigured build simply has no send-later, rather than silently dropping mail.

### Calendar (only when `[caldav] enabled`)

Times are RFC 3339 strings. The `start`/`end` range defaults to the current
month when omitted. These reuse the same CalDAV client + `models.Calendar*`
types as the React calendar UI.

| Method | Path | Query | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|-------|------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/v1/calendar/events`          | `start`, `end` | —          | `{ events: CalendarEvent[] }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/calendar/events`          | —              | `{ summary, start, end, description?, location?, allDay?, recurrence? }` | `201 { created: true }` |
| `PUT`    | `/v1/calendar/events/:uid`     | —              | `{ summary, start, end, description?, location?, allDay?, recurrence?, path? }` | `{ updated: true }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/calendar/events/:uid`     | —              | —          | `204` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/calendar/freebusy`        | `start`, `end` | —          | `{ busy: { start, end }[] }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/calendar/rsvp`            | —              | `{ uid, organizer, response, …event }` | `{ ok: true }` |

`recurrence` is a raw iCalendar RRULE (e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10`), stored and
returned verbatim. `CalendarEvent` includes `uid`, `path` (CalDAV object path)
and `recurrence`; pass `path` back on `PUT` so an edit targets the exact object.

`POST /v1/calendar/rsvp` is the **iTIP/iMIP** reply to a received invitation: it
sends a `METHOD:REPLY` back to the `organizer` with the chosen `response`
(`ACCEPTED` / `DECLINED` / `TENTATIVE`) and reflects the event into the
responder's own calendar. A received invite arrives on a message as
`Email.Invite` (attendees plus the recipient's own `MyPartStat`), which the client
reads from `GET /v1/messages/:uid`.

### Contacts (only when `[carddav] enabled`)

Everything here reads and writes the **user's own** CardDAV address book. There
is no inbrix-side contact database: a card exists iff it exists on the user's
CardDAV server, so two inbrix instances pointed at one account see one book.

| Method | Path | Query | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|-------|------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/v1/contacts`                 | `q`, `limit` (50)  | —       | `{ contacts: { email, name }[] }` (autocomplete form) |
| `GET`    | `/v1/contacts/cards`           | `q`, `limit` (500), `group` | — | `{ contacts: Contact[] }` (full cards) |
| `GET`    | `/v1/contacts/frequent`        | `limit` (12, max 50) | —     | `{ contacts: { email, name?, count, lastUsed }[] }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/contacts`                 | —                  | `Contact` (no `uid`/`path`) | `201 { contact }` |
| `PUT`    | `/v1/contacts/:uid`            | —                  | `Contact` (`path?` targets the exact object) | `{ contact }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/contacts/:uid`            | `path?`            | —       | `204` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/contacts/:uid/photo`      | —                  | multipart form, file field `file` | `{ contact }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/contacts/:uid/photo`      | —                  | —       | `{ contact }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/contacts/groups`          | —                  | —       | `{ groups: { name, count }[] }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/contacts/groups`          | —                  | `{ name }` | `201 { group: { name, count: 0 } }` |
| `PATCH`  | `/v1/contacts/groups/:name`    | —                  | `{ name }` | `{ renamed: <cards rewritten>, name }` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/contacts/groups/:name`    | —                  | —       | `{ removed: <cards rewritten> }` |
| `POST`   | `/v1/contacts/import`          | —                  | multipart form: `file`, `format?`, `mapping?` | `{ imported, skipped }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/contacts/export`          | `format` (`vcf`\|`csv`) | —  | file download (`text/vcard` / `text/csv`) |

The literal sub-paths (`cards`, `frequent`, `groups`, `import`, `export`) are
registered **before** `/v1/contacts/:uid`, so they are never captured as a UID.

When the account has no usable CardDAV target — standalone with `[carddav]`
unconfigured, or an injected-credential request with no
`X-Vulos-Mail-Carddav-Url` — **reads degrade to an empty result** (`{"contacts":
[]}` / `{"groups": []}`) and **writes return `501 Not Implemented`** with
`{"error":"contacts not available for this account"}`. Nothing falls back to a
different account's book.

#### `Contact` shape

`GET /v1/contacts/cards` returns these verbatim, and `POST`/`PUT` accept the same
shape. Only `uid`, `name` and `emails` are always present; every other field is
omitted when empty.

```jsonc
{
  "uid": "8f14e45f-ea4c-4b1e-9b06-9f2b3c0a1d77", // vCard UID, server-assigned on create
  "name": "Alice Adams",                          // vCard FN
  "structuredName": {                             // vCard N; derived from name when absent
    "prefix": "Dr", "first": "Alice", "middle": "Q", "last": "Adams", "suffix": "PhD"
  },
  "nickname": "Al",
  "fileAs": "Adams, Alice",                       // SORT-AS / X-ABShowAs list-ordering hint
  "org": "Example Ltd",
  "department": "Platform",                       // ORG component 2
  "title": "Staff Engineer",
  "note": "met at FOSDEM",
  "emails": ["alice@example.com"],                // unlabelled projection (always present)
  "phones": ["+44 20 7946 0000"],
  "typedEmails": [{ "value": "alice@example.com", "type": "work" }],
  "typedPhones": [{ "value": "+44 20 7946 0000", "type": "mobile" }],
  "addresses": [{ "type": "home", "poBox": "", "extended": "", "street": "1 High St",
                  "locality": "London", "region": "", "postal": "SW1A 1AA", "country": "GB" }],
  "websites": [{ "value": "https://example.com", "type": "work" }],
  "ims":      [{ "value": "alice@xmpp.example", "type": "xmpp" }],
  "birthday": "1990-04-01",                       // ISO date or the vCard raw value
  "anniversary": "2015-06-20",
  "groups": ["Team", "Conference"],               // CATEGORIES membership
  "photo": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KG…",    // raster data URI only (see below)
  "starred": true,
  "path": "/dav/addressbooks/user/default/8f14e45f.vcf" // CardDAV object path
}
```

- **`typedEmails`/`typedPhones` are authoritative when present**; `emails`/`phones`
  are then derived from them. A lean client may send only `emails`/`phones`.
- **`starred`** is stored as a reserved `CATEGORIES` value so it round-trips
  through CardDAV like any other group, but it is surfaced as a boolean and is
  **hidden from `/v1/contacts/groups`** — you cannot create or rename a group to
  the reserved starred name (the request is a `400`).
- **`photo`** is accepted **only** as a `data:` URI holding a PNG, JPEG, GIF or
  WebP, is content-sniffed (not trusted from the declared type), and is capped at
  **2 MiB**. An SVG, an HTML payload, or a bare `http(s)://` URL is dropped
  server-side rather than stored — so a hostile card can never carry a
  stored-XSS vector or a tracking beacon into a client that renders it.
- **Bounds** (silently clamped, never a `500`): 1024 chars per scalar field, 8192
  for `note`, 512 per email/phone/URL/IM value, 64 items per typed collection,
  128 groups per card, 128 chars per group name, 64 chars per `type` label.
- `POST` ignores any client-sent `uid`/`path` and always mints a fresh UID.
  Both `POST` and `PUT` require at least a name **or** one email (`400` otherwise).

#### Photos

`POST /v1/contacts/:uid/photo` takes a multipart form with a `file` field, runs
the same raster/size gate as the JSON path, attaches the result to the card, and
returns the saved `{ contact }`. `DELETE` clears it and likewise returns the saved
card. An over-cap upload is `413`; a non-raster image is `415`; an unknown `uid`
is `404`.

#### Groups (labels)

Groups are modelled **entirely** inside each card's `CATEGORIES` property (the
Google/Apple convention) — there is no separate group store, so a group exists
iff some card in the book carries it, and group state is per-account by
construction.

- **Assign / unassign is done through the normal contact `PUT`**: edit
  `contact.groups` and save. There is deliberately no assign endpoint.
- `POST /v1/contacts/groups` makes a brand-new (empty) group visible by writing a
  hidden placeholder card carrying only that category. Placeholder cards are
  filtered out of `/v1/contacts/cards`, `/v1/contacts/export` and group counts,
  and are deleted automatically once the group is removed from them. A duplicate
  name (case-insensitive) is `409`.
- `PATCH` rewrites the category on every card that carries it and reports how many
  cards changed; `DELETE` drops the membership from every card but **keeps the
  cards themselves**.

#### Import / export

`POST /v1/contacts/import` accepts a `.vcf` (one or many vCards) or a `.csv`
(Google/Outlook export shape). `format` may be `vcf` or `csv`; when omitted it is
sniffed from the filename, then from the content (`BEGIN:VCARD`). `mapping` is an
optional `field:index,field:index` override applied on top of the auto-matched CSV
header — useful after the client previews the header row. Recognised mapping
fields: `name`, `first`, `middle`, `last`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `nickname`,
`email`, `phone`, `org`, `department`, `title`, `note`, `website`, `birthday`,
`groups`, `starred`, `photo`.

Import is **bounded and forgiving**: the upload is capped at **10 MiB** (`413`
past that), at most **5000** contacts are created per request, every row is
sanitized through the same gate as a JSON write, and a malformed or
identity-less row is counted in `skipped` rather than failing the whole import.
Imported UIDs are always discarded and re-minted. The response is
`{ "imported": <n>, "skipped": <n> }`.

`GET /v1/contacts/export?format=vcf` (default) streams `text/vcard`;
`format=csv` streams `text/csv` with the fixed column set *Name, Given Name,
Family Name, Nickname, Organization, Department, Title, E-mail 1, Phone 1,
Website 1, Birthday, Notes, Groups, Starred, Photo* — a superset that re-imports
cleanly. CSV export is **formula-injection guarded**: any cell starting with
`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR is prefixed with `'` so a hostile contact field
cannot execute when the export is opened in Excel/Sheets.

#### Frequently contacted

`GET /v1/contacts/frequent` is **not** a CardDAV read. It exposes the local
recent-recipients store that the send path already appends to after every send,
ordered by (`count` desc, `lastUsed` desc). It is read-only and per-account: the
store file is keyed by the request's own sanitized username under
`[cache] folder` — the exact path the send path writes to. Where there is no
local store (a brokered account whose sends were never recorded locally, or
`[cache] folder` unset) it returns an empty list rather than an error.

### Settings — vacation responder (`/v1/settings/vacation`)

Per-account out-of-office responder config. Durable-KV backed — returns `501`
when no store is wired. Owner is the authenticated identity (session email or
injected-credential mailbox); a caller only ever reads/writes **their own** config.

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/v1/settings/vacation` | — | `VacationConfig` |
| `PUT` | `/v1/settings/vacation` | `VacationConfig` | `VacationConfig` |

```jsonc
// VacationConfig
{
  "enabled": true,
  "subject": "Out of office",       // becomes a real mail Subject → CR/LF/NUL rejected (400)
  "body": "<p>Back Monday</p>",     // HTML, sanitized server-side (script/handlers/js: stripped)
  "startAt": "2026-07-10T00:00:00Z", // optional RFC3339; responder inactive before this
  "endAt":   "2026-07-20T00:00:00Z", // optional RFC3339; inactive after this; must be ≥ startAt
  "respondOnlyToContacts": false     // limit auto-replies to known contacts (anti-backscatter)
}
```

An enabled responder requires a non-empty `subject`. The body is sanitized (a
stored-XSS payload cannot ride the auto-reply). Loop/backscatter protection is
built in: auto-replies are never sent to another auto-reply (`Auto-Submitted`),
to list mail (`List-*` / `Precedence: bulk`), or to a null/bounce sender.

**Enforcement note:** inbrix is a **client** — it connects to the user's provider
over IMAP/SMTP and does **not** run the inbound delivery path, so storing
`enabled:true` here does not by itself make the provider auto-reply. This endpoint
is the authoritative **config** the client edits and stores; actual enforcement
must be set on the provider's own vacation/out-of-office feature (Gmail, Fastmail,
a self-hosted Dovecot/Sieve, …). The GET always echoes the stored config so the UI
stays truthful about what it holds.

### Settings — signatures (`/v1/settings/signatures`)

Multiple named HTML signatures. `PUT` replaces the whole set. Each signature's
HTML is sanitized. The server assigns an `id` when omitted (create by omitting).
At most one signature may be `default:true`.

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/v1/settings/signatures` | — | `{ signatures: Signature[] }` |
| `PUT` | `/v1/settings/signatures` | `{ signatures: Signature[] }` | `{ signatures: Signature[] }` |

```jsonc
// Signature
{ "id": "a1b2c3d4", "name": "Work", "html": "<b>Jane Doe</b>", "default": true }
```

### Settings — quick reply templates (`/v1/settings/reply-templates`)

Quick reply templates for the compose and reply modals. `PUT` replaces the whole set.
The server assigns an `id` when omitted. `configured: false` indicates the account has
never saved templates yet (allowing clients to present localized default templates).

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/v1/settings/reply-templates` | — | `{ templates: ReplyTemplate[], configured: boolean }` |
| `PUT` | `/v1/settings/reply-templates` | `{ templates: ReplyTemplate[] }` | `{ templates: ReplyTemplate[], configured: boolean }` |

```jsonc
// ReplyTemplate
{ "id": "b2c3d4e5", "name": "Acknowledge receipt", "body": "Thank you for your email..." }
```

### System settings and roles (`/api/system`)

Application accounts have role `user` or `super_admin`. New and migrated users
default to `user`. These session-authenticated endpoints require
`super_admin`; ordinary users receive `403` even if they call the endpoints
directly. Password hashes are never returned.

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/api/public/settings` | — | `{ registrationOpen }` (public) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/settings` | — | `{ version, currentUserId, registrationOpen, users: SystemUser[] }` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/system/settings/registration` | `{ "registrationOpen": boolean }` | `{ registrationOpen }` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/system/users/:id/role` | `{ "role": "user" | "super_admin" }` | Updated `SystemUser` |

A super administrator may change another user's role but cannot demote its own
account. `/api/capabilities` includes the current account's `role`, which the UI
uses to hide the System settings entry from ordinary users; server-side checks
remain authoritative.

Registration is open by default for backward compatibility. Closing it hides
the registration entry points in the browser and makes `POST /register` return
`403`; the server-side check remains authoritative.

### Settings — send-as identities (`/v1/settings/identities`)

The From/identity list the compose window offers. The primary mailbox is **always**
returned first with `isPrimary:true` (never removable), followed by any send-as
aliases. Each identity may link a default signature by id.

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/v1/settings/identities` | — | `{ identities: Identity[] }` |
| `PUT` | `/v1/settings/identities` | `{ identities: Identity[] }` | `{ identities: Identity[] }` |

`PUT` **replaces the whole set of aliases**. The primary mailbox is implicit: it is
never stored, never writable, and always re-added on read.

**inbrix is a client, not the send-as authority.** These identities are the
**client's read model** — the list the compose window offers. The user's own
provider SMTP server remains the authority for what From it will actually accept,
and re-checks it at submission time. Each address is still validated locally for
shape and header-injection (CR/LF/NUL in the address or name ⇒ `400`) before it is
stored. Nothing here makes an address inbound-deliverable — inbound delivery is the
provider's concern, not inbrix's.

Compose honours the choice: `POST /v1/messages` (and `/v1/drafts`) accept
`"from": "<address>"`, which must be the primary mailbox or a **registered**
identity — anything else is `403` (and the provider's SMTP server re-checks it at
submission). A scheduled send fires with that From but the record stays **owned**
by the authenticated mailbox.

```jsonc
// Identity
{ "address": "me@example.com", "name": "Me", "isPrimary": true, "defaultSignatureId": "a1b2c3d4" }
```

### Connected accounts + unified inbox (`/v1/accounts`, `/v1/unified`)

Additional mailboxes the user has connected, and a merged read across all of them.
Durable-KV backed (`501` without a store). Credentials are **AES-GCM encrypted at
rest** with the app key and are **never** returned in any response. Strict
per-user isolation: a user lists/adds/removes/reads only their own accounts;
another user's account is `404` (no-leak).

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/v1/accounts`         | — | `{ accounts: ConnectedAccount[] }` (no secrets) |
| `POST`   | `/v1/accounts`         | `AddAccount` | `201 ConnectedAccount` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/accounts/:id`     | — | `204` (own) / `404` (foreign or missing) |
| `GET`    | `/v1/unified`          | `?folder=&limit=` | `{ folder, messages: Email[], errors: [] }` |
| `GET`    | `/v1/messages?account=all` | `?folder=&limit=` | same as `/v1/unified` (alias) |

```jsonc
// AddAccount (POST body) — password validated against the live IMAP server first
{ "email":"work@corp.com", "password":"…", "label":"Work", "color":"#0a0",
  "imapServer":"imap.corp.com", "imapPort":993, "smtpServer":"smtp.corp.com", "smtpPort":587 }

// ConnectedAccount (response) — password fields OMITTED, never serialized
{ "id":"acct_…", "email":"work@corp.com", "label":"Work", "color":"#0a0",
  "imapServer":"imap.corp.com", "imapPort":993, "smtpServer":"smtp.corp.com", "smtpPort":587 }
```

The unified fetch runs one connection per account concurrently (each with its own
timeout); **one failing account never breaks the others** — its failure appears in
the `errors` array (`{account, error}`) alongside the messages that did load. Each
merged message is tagged with its source via `accountEmail` / `accountLabel` /
`accountColor` on the `Email` shape, and the list is newest-first, capped at 200.

### Examples

```bash
# List mailboxes
curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:2342/v1/folders

# 50 most recent messages in INBOX
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages?folder=INBOX&limit=50'

# Read one message
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages/42?folder=INBOX'

# Full-text search
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/search?folder=INBOX&q=invoice'

# Mark as read (\Seen)  /  star (\Flagged)
curl -b cookies.txt -X PATCH 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages/42/flags?folder=INBOX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"flag":"\\Seen","add":true}'

# Delete (moves to Trash by default)
curl -b cookies.txt -X DELETE 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages/42?folder=INBOX'

# Permanently delete (expunge, skip Trash)
curl -b cookies.txt -X DELETE 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages/42?folder=INBOX&hard=true'

# Move / archive a message
curl -b cookies.txt -X POST 'http://localhost:2342/v1/messages/42/move?folder=INBOX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"toFolder":"Archive"}'

# Send a message
curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:2342/v1/messages \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"to":"alice@example.com","subject":"Hi","text":"Hello from /v1"}'

# Save a draft
curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:2342/v1/drafts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"to":"alice@example.com","subject":"WIP","text":"unfinished…"}'

# List calendar events for a range (CalDAV must be enabled)
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/calendar/events?start=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z&end=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z'

# Search contacts (CardDAV must be enabled)
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/contacts?q=alice'

# Set the vacation responder
curl -b cookies.txt -X PUT http://localhost:2342/v1/settings/vacation \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"enabled":true,"subject":"Out of office","body":"<p>Back Monday</p>"}'

# Add a connected account (password is validated against IMAP, then encrypted at rest)
curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:2342/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"work@corp.com","password":"…","label":"Work","imapServer":"imap.corp.com"}'

# Unified inbox across the primary + all connected accounts
curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:2342/v1/unified?folder=INBOX&limit=50'
```

### `Email` shape (abridged)

```jsonc
{
  "id": "42",
  "from": "alice@example.com",
  "fromName": "Alice",
  "to": "me@example.com",
  "toNames": ["Me"],
  "cc": "bob@example.com",
  "subject": "Invoice",
  "preview": "Here is the invoice you asked for…",
  "body": "plain text body",
  "html": "<p>…</p>",
  "date": "2026-06-26T10:00:00Z",
  "hasAttachments": true,
  "attachments": [
    {
      "id": "SU5CT1gAMzQAMi4x",   // opaque attachment identifier
      "partId": "2.1",             // IMAP MIME part path — use with the /v1 download route
      "filename": "invoice.pdf",
      "contentType": "application/pdf",
      "size": 84320,
      "isInline": false
    }
  ],
  "flags": ["\\Seen"],
  "messageId": "<…@example.com>",
  "inReplyTo": "<…>",
  "references": ["<…>"],
  "accountEmail": "work@corp.com",   // only in unified results — source account tag
  "accountLabel": "Work",
  "accountColor": "#0a0",
  "auth": {                           // only on a single-message read; omitted if no header
    "spf": "pass",                    // pass|fail|softfail|neutral|none|temperror|permerror
    "dkim": "pass",
    "dmarc": "pass",
    "dkimDomain": "sender.com",
    "raw": "mx.example.com; spf=pass …" // verbatim Authentication-Results value
  },
  "invite": { … },                    // present iff the message carries a text/calendar iMIP part
  "unsubscribe": {                    // present iff the message advertises List-Unsubscribe
    "httpUrl": "https://example.com/u/abc",
    "mailtoUrl": "mailto:unsub@example.com?subject=unsub",
    "oneClick": true
  },
  "brand": {                          // present iff DMARC passed AND the domain publishes BIMI
    "domain": "sender.com",
    "logo": "data:image/svg+xml;base64,…",
    "vmc": true
  }
}
```

`invite` (nil for ordinary mail) is the parsed iTIP/iMIP invitation — attendees
plus the recipient's own `MyPartStat` — and is what the client answers with
`POST /v1/calendar/rsvp`.

`unsubscribe` is the parsed `List-Unsubscribe` (RFC 2369) pair. **inbrix never
unsubscribes on your behalf** — it only surfaces the targets. Only `http`,
`https` and `mailto` schemes are ever emitted; anything else is dropped so a
hostile scheme cannot ride through to the client. `oneClick` is true only when
the sender also sent `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` (RFC
8058) **and** an `httpUrl` exists, meaning the client may POST
`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` to `httpUrl` directly.

`brand` is a **verified** sender brand logo (BIMI) and is **fail-closed**: it is
populated only when the message carries a DMARC `pass` verdict *and* the From
domain publishes a BIMI record whose logo inbrix fetched (SSRF-screened) and
sanitized. An unauthenticated sender therefore never gets a logo, so its presence
is only ever a positive trust signal, never a phishing aid. `logo` is a sanitized
SVG `data:` URI safe to place in an `<img src>`. `vmc` reflects only that the
record referenced a Verified Mark Certificate (`a=` tag) — the certificate chain
is **not** validated, so treat it as informational. Resolution is served from a
per-domain cache and warmed in the background on a miss, so the first read of a
message from a new domain may return no `brand` even though one exists; a
subsequent read returns it.

`attachments[]` is metadata only (no bytes). Build a download link as
`/v1/messages/{id}/attachments/{partId}?folder={folder}`. `isInline` flags parts
meant to render inline (e.g. embedded images) versus regular file attachments.

`auth` (present on a single-message read, `GET /v1/messages/:uid`) surfaces the
**receiving server's** SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdict, parsed read-only from the message's
`Authentication-Results` header (RFC 8601). inbrix does not re-verify; it exposes
the trusted receiver's stamp so the client can render a "verified sender" / "why in
spam" badge. `null`/absent when the message carries no such header.

## Demo mode

When `[demo] enabled = true`, the API is backed by the in-memory `DemoClient`
(no IMAP contact), so it returns seeded data — useful for building/screenshotting
clients without a live mailbox.

## Not yet exposed

Recurring-event expansion (server-side RRULE materialization) is not yet exposed
over `/v1`. Track this in [ROADMAP.md](roadmap.md).

## Skills

Settings → **Skills** manages reusable workflows. These APIs accept either
`Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` or `X-API-Key: <API_KEY>` and inherit the current
user's permissions. Skills and the active summary workflow are isolated by owner.
Browser mutations retain the normal CSRF requirement.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/settings/ai/skills` | List skills and `mailSummarySkillId`. |
| POST | `/api/settings/ai/skills` | Create a skill. |
| GET | `/api/settings/ai/skills/:id` | Read one skill, including its instructions and revision. |
| PUT | `/api/settings/ai/skills/:id` | Update editable fields; omitted fields are preserved. |
| PATCH | `/api/settings/ai/skills/:id` | Partially update a skill. |
| DELETE | `/api/settings/ai/skills/:id` | Delete an unused skill; optional `?revision=N` checks its revision. |
| POST | `/api/settings/ai/skills/:id/use-for-mail-summary` | Select an enabled mail-summary skill for all the owner's mailboxes. |

Create body:

```json
{
  "id": "customer-follow-up",
  "name": "Customer follow-up",
  "description": "Track unanswered requests using source emails",
  "kind": "chat",
  "instructions": "Read the latest email and relevant history. Identify open questions and next actions, with email sources.",
  "dependsOn": ["email_analysis"],
  "enabled": true
}
```

`id` is optional and generated when blank; explicit ids use lowercase letters,
digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter (at most 64 characters).
`name` and `instructions` are required. `kind` is `chat` (default) or
`mail_summary` and cannot change after creation. `description`, `dependsOn` and
`enabled` default to an empty string, empty array and true. Instructions are
limited to 16,000 UTF-8 bytes, names to 100 characters, descriptions to 400
characters, dependencies to 12, and the registry to 64 skills. Each enabled
skill's expanded dependency instructions have a 24,000-byte context budget.
Chat supplies a bounded metadata catalog and loads full instructions only for
the selected skill or through `load_skill`; unique root loads have a cumulative
48,000-byte instruction budget per execution. Other runtime limits still apply.

Responses include `revision`, `builtIn`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. PATCH/PUT
accept editable fields and an optional positive `revision`; a stale revision
returns **409**. Include the revision from GET to protect against overwriting
an editor's changes. Successful saves increment the revision. Unknown JSON keys
are rejected; do not send read-only response fields back as updates.

Only current Skill content is stored. `revision` is a lightweight concurrency
check, not a historical version API. Deleting a Skill removes its configuration;
recreating the same id starts at revision 1. Saves apply to subsequent executions.
Upgrading removes the former history archive; active content, dependency bindings
and existing execution snapshots are preserved.

```sh
curl "$INBRIX_URL/api/settings/ai/skills/customer-follow-up" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INBRIX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X PATCH --data '{"revision":1,"instructions":"Verify each unanswered request against the latest source emails."}'
```

To create an alternative automatic-summary workflow, use `kind=mail_summary`,
then POST its `use-for-mail-summary` endpoint with `{ "revision": 1 }`. This
workflow applies to all the owner's mailboxes; mailbox model, business prompt
and task-enable settings still apply. Automatic summaries use free text of at
most 200 Unicode characters including punctuation, without fixed output labels. Dependencies must exist in
the same owner's registry, match the skill's kind, and be acyclic. An enabled
skill cannot depend on a disabled skill. An active summary cannot be deleted or disabled; any referenced skill cannot
be deleted, and a dependency of an enabled skill cannot be disabled (**409**).

Default workflows (`email_analysis`, `quotation`, `contract`, `mail-analysis`)
are seeded once per owner and can be edited. Deleting an unused built-in does
not restore it on restart. Enabled chat skills appear in both chat selectors.
Each turn freezes the current catalog, injects the explicitly selected skill
and its dependencies, and exposes `load_skill` for other matching workflows.
Automatic summaries read their selected skill and
dependencies for each new run; changed revisions mark existing summaries stale
without silently replacing them. A run already in progress retains its loaded
snapshot. Skills are declarative instructions: tool implementations, account
access, brand restrictions and output validation remain enforced by server code.

## Mail background tasks

These endpoints support browser sessions and API Keys, with the same owner and
mailbox checks as other AI settings APIs. They inspect work queued by incremental
mail synchronization; they do not enqueue history or replay successful delivery.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/settings/ai/mail-tasks` | Read current task status. Required: `accountEmail`; optional: `folder`, `messageId`, `limit` (1–100, default 50). |
| GET | `/api/settings/ai/mail-tasks/runs` | Read attempt history, newest first. Same query fields, plus optional `taskType` (`analysis`, `reply`, `notification`). Returns `{ "runs": [...] }`. |
| POST | `/api/settings/ai/mail-tasks/retry` | Retry a terminal failed task. Body: `accountEmail`, `folder`, `messageId`, `taskType`. Ready notifications cannot be replayed. |

Each attempt has a distinct public `id`, `folder`, `messageId`, `taskType`,
`attempt`, `status`, `phase`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, `durationMs`, `errorKind`,
`error`, `retryable`, and `context`. Run statuses are `running`, `ready`, `skipped`,
`failed`, `interrupted`, or `expired`. A failed run with `retryable=true` means
the queue scheduled another attempt; check the task's current status and
`nextAttempt` for its present state. Explicit retries reset the task's attempt
counter but retain previous run records. Shutdown interruptions do not consume
the failure budget. Public ids are separate from internal fencing tokens.

Run context includes the model id/name/provider and config fingerprint when
generation was reached, plus Skill ids/revisions and their combined fingerprint
for mail analysis. `cached` and `stale` distinguish reused results; cached version
metadata describes the stored result, not the current configuration. Full prompts,
notification payloads, mail bodies, credentials and fencing-token fields are
excluded. Each task retains at most 50 run records, removed when its email is
deleted. No history is fabricated for attempts made before this feature.

Background AI execution is serialized per mailbox and capped at four simultaneous
tasks across the database. Notification delivery has a separate per-mailbox lane:
it waits for the corresponding first analysis attempt, or becomes eligible for a
basic notification after 30 seconds from enqueue. Scheduling polls every five
seconds and wakes on completed work, so this is a summary-wait threshold, not a
remote-delivery deadline. Interactive chat/manual model requests are outside this
background cap.

Transient retries use exponential backoff with jitter. HTTP 429 respects
`Retry-After`; HTTP 401/403 and other non-retryable 4xx require explicit retry
after repair. Structured mail-analysis output validation gets one additional
attempt. Duplicate remote delivery remains possible when an acknowledgement is
lost; successful tasks are never replayed by the retry endpoint.

## Business assistants and built-in Skills

Existing `/api/settings/ai/agents` records now accept and return `businessProfile`:

```json
{
  "name": "Valve sales assistant",
  "prompt": "Use concise language and clarify missing requirements.",
  "outputLabels": ["客户", "需求"],
  "businessProfile": {
    "company": "Seller Ltd",
    "quotationTemplateId": "default-quotation",
    "contractTemplateId": "default-contract"
  }
}
```

Brand responsibilities belong to mailboxes, configured under Settings → Mailboxes → Edit → Mailbox brands:

- GET `/api/accounts/:id/brands` returns `{ "brands": ["Brand A", "Brand B"], "brandMode": "restrict" }`.
- PUT the same shape to update; both operations require mailbox ownership. An unconfigured mailbox returns empty brands with `prefer` mode. Clearing brands is allowed in `prefer` mode.
- All assistants for this mailbox use the latest binding on every chat turn. Switching assistants preserves the conversation's explicit brand selection.
- On first upgrade, brands from the mailbox's bound email-draft assistant are copied once. Legacy assistant brand fields remain stored for compatibility but no longer affect prompts or scope; unbound mailboxes start unrestricted.

`brandMode=prefer` uses brands as defaults when the customer has not specified
one; other explicitly requested brands remain accessible. `restrict` requires at
least one brand and enforces the allowed brands in catalog search (before
pagination), direct product reads, price queries, generated document items and
proposed item updates. Scoped document lines must reference actual catalog
products. A conversation may narrow this range, never widen it. Brands match
exactly as stored in the product library. This configuration governs business
catalog usage; it does not change the signed-in user's mailbox/document access.

Templates must belong to the current user and match the document type. Empty
ids use the system template; built-in ids are `default-quotation` and
`default-contract`. Saved custom canvas templates retain their layout and editor
options, fill structured controls, expand product rows, and clear old buyer/item
values. Legacy plain HTML templates must first be saved through the canvas
editor. A deleted custom default produces an actionable error rather than a
silent layout substitution. PUT requests that omit `businessProfile` preserve the stored
profile.

GET `/api/settings/ai/agents` also returns a `skills` catalog (id, name,
description, dependsOn). This is the enabled chat subset of the managed
Skills registry. Default declarative workflows are:

| Skill | Workflow |
| --- | --- |
| `email_analysis` | Read mail sources; extract per-line brands, specifications, quantities and missing requirements. |
| `quotation` | Compose email analysis, verify technical suitability and catalog configurations/prices, prepare a quotation draft. |
| `contract` | Verify the designated quotation and contract terms; compose selection/quotation when new prices are needed. |

POST `/api/ai/agent-chat` accepts this optional selection:

```json
{
  "businessContext": {
    "agentId": "aiagent_...",
    "skillId": "quotation",
    "brands": ["Brand A"]
  }
}
```

Empty `skillId` automatically selects/composes the built-in workflows; empty
`brands` inherits mailbox defaults. A nonempty selection is an explicit catalog
filter. `agentId` remains a legacy request alias; invalid assistants or Skill ids
are rejected. Mailbox email-draft bindings remain the default assistant when no
assistant is selected. The response (including SSE `done.response`) returns the
resolved `businessContext`. Identity/default data is separate from the workflow
instructions and current catalog facts. Text in mail/product data is treated as
reference material, not instructions.

For a mail conversation, the context is stored separately from derived AI
summaries in SQLite. GET `/api/conversations/:id/ai-chat` returns it beside
`messages`, `sessionId`, `version` and `lastRun`. PUT accepts only
`{version, businessContext}`; obsolete full-history writes are rejected with 409.
Deleting chat history requires `?version=...` and clears messages and derived
summaries while retaining business context. Each subsequent agent turn resolves
the latest mailbox restrictions. Document drafting uses the same server session
store, scoped to the authenticated owner and selected mailbox. The document library's
**Draft with AI** action opens this workspace; `/ai-document` also opens it.

`read_document` returns the saved document's `revision`. `generate_document`
accepts `sourceQuotationId` and `sourceQuotationRevision` for `type=contract`.
A supplied revision must match the owner's saved quotation; otherwise the tool
asks the agent to read and confirm it again. If omitted by an older caller, the
current revision is captured on first use. The server reads that owner's saved
structured quotation once per generated contract and copies its buyer, item
configuration, quantities, prices, amounts and commercial fields. Current catalog
prices do not replace this commercial snapshot. The same immutable snapshot is
used through final reply processing, even if the source is edited or deleted
while the model is replying. A final document fence cannot replace a contract
